blocks.prompt: 9. Find the general solution of the differential equation \(y - x\frac{dy}{dx} = 2\left(y^2 + \frac{dy}{dx}\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) do jagah aaya hai, is liye pehle usay ek jagah ikattha karna hai.
Ikattha karne par \((x + 2)\frac{dy}{dx} = y - 2y^2\) milta hai: ek taraf sirf \(x\), doosri taraf sirf \(y\). Yani separable.
Find kya karna hai? General solution.
Plan: alag karenge, \(\frac{1}{y(1 - 2y)}\) ko partial fractions mein torenge, integrate kar ke logs jorenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y - x\frac{dy}{dx} = 2\left(y^2 + \frac{dy}{dx}\right)\).
Maloom karna: general solution.
Tareeqa: Pehle saari \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) wali terms ek taraf jama karenge; equation separable ban jayegi. \(y\) wali side ke liye partial fractions lagenge.

\(\frac{dy}{dx}\) wali terms ikatthi karein
\[y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2y^2 + 2\dfrac{dy}{dx}\]
\[y - 2y^2 = (x + 2)\dfrac{dy}{dx}\]
Kyun: Pehle bracket khola. Phir \(2y^2\) ko left par aur \(-x\frac{dy}{dx}\) ko right par bheja; right par \(x\frac{dy}{dx} + 2\frac{dy}{dx} = (x + 2)\frac{dy}{dx}\) common nikal kar likha.
Dhyan dein: Bracket kholte waqt 2 ko dono terms se multiply karna hai, sirf \(y^2\) se nahi.

Variables alag karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{y(1 - 2y)} = \dfrac{dx}{x + 2}\]
Kyun: \(y - 2y^2\) mein \(y\) common nikala: \(y(1 - 2y)\). Phir dono taraf \(y(1 - 2y)\) aur \(x + 2\) se divide kiya.

Partial fractions
\[\dfrac{1}{y(1 - 2y)} = \dfrac{A}{y} + \dfrac{B}{1 - 2y}\]
\[1 = A(1 - 2y) + By\]
\(y = 0\) rakhein: \(A = 1\). \(y = \frac{1}{2}\) rakhein: \(1 = \frac{B}{2}\), to \(B = 2\).
Kyun: \(y = 0\) se \(By\) wali term zero, aur \(y = \frac{1}{2}\) se \(A(1 - 2y)\) wali term zero ho jati hai; har dafa ek constant seedha mil jata hai.

Dono taraf integrate karein
\[\int\left(\dfrac{1}{y} + \dfrac{2}{1 - 2y}\right)dy = \int\dfrac{dx}{x + 2}\]
\[\ln|y| - \ln|1 - 2y| = \ln|x + 2| + \ln|C|\]
Kyun: \(1 - 2y\) ki derivative \(-2\) hai, is liye \(\int\frac{2\,dy}{1 - 2y} = -\ln|1 - 2y|\). Right side par \(\ln|x + 2|\). Constant ko \(\ln|C|\) likha taake sab logs jur sakein.
Dhyan dein: Yahan minus bhoolne se jawab \(y(1 - 2y)\) jaisa ghalat ban jata hai.

Logs jorein aur hatayein
\[\ln\left|\dfrac{y}{1 - 2y}\right| = \ln|C(x + 2)|\]
\[\dfrac{y}{1 - 2y} = C(x + 2)\]
\[y = C(x + 2)(1 - 2y)\]
Kyun: \(\ln a - \ln b = \ln\frac{a}{b}\) aur \(\ln a + \ln b = \ln ab\). Logs barabar hon to andar wali cheezein barabar. Absolute value se aane wala \(\pm\) constant \(C\) mein shamil ho gaya.

Tasdeeq
\(\frac{y}{1 - 2y} = C(x + 2)\) ko differentiate karein:
\[\dfrac{1}{(1 - 2y)^2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = C = \dfrac{y}{(1 - 2y)(x + 2)}\]
\[(x + 2)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y(1 - 2y) = y - 2y^2\]
Kyun: Quotient rule se \(\frac{y}{1 - 2y}\) ki derivative \(\frac{1}{(1 - 2y)^2}\frac{dy}{dx}\) aati hai. \(C\) ki jagah us ki value rakhi aur asal equation wapas mil gayi.
Kitab ka jawab \(y = C(x + 2)(2y - 1)\) bhi sahi hai: \((2y - 1) = -(1 - 2y)\), aur \(-C\) bhi bas ek constant hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(y = C(x + 2)(1 - 2y)\); kitab ki shakal \(y = C(x + 2)(2y - 1)\) bhi yahi khandaan hai (\(C\) ki jagah \(-C\)).
